resolution_semantics.published_route: native 2704x2028 PNGs decoded by pre_n3d.py (cv2, downscale=1), COLMAP intrinsics at 2704x2028, config resolution:2 -> utils/camera_utils.py halves to 1352x1014 for train AND eval.
resolution_semantics.adags_derived_route: derived frames are ALREADY 1352x1014, so prep passes --downscale 2 to convertdynerftocolmapdb (COLMAP intrinsics 1352x1014, focal 731.0336 = 1462.0671/2) and the config must set resolution:1. Both routes train and evaluate at 1352x1014 with identical field of view.
resolution_semantics.trap: using the stock configs/n3d_full/*.json on the derived frames would train at 676x507 -- a quarter of the published pixel count.

test_rendering.where: test.py render_set() -> torchvision.utils.save_image(rendering, <model_path>/test/ours_<iteration>/renders/{idx:05d}.png) at test.py:147; ground truth to .../gt/{idx:05d}.png at test.py:148
test_rendering.which_camera: with --eval and --valloader colmapvalid, scene/dataset_readers.py:792-793 sets test_cam_infos = cam_infos[:duration] after sorting by image_name, and asserts exactly one distinct camera name. On N3V that is cam00, positionally. Train cameras are the remaining 20 on flame_steak.
test_rendering.frame_index_mapping: idx 0..duration-1 corresponds to absolute frames starttime..starttime+duration-1, where starttime is parsed from the colmap_<starttime> directory name (dataset_readers.py:784).
test_rendering.metrics_written: <model_path>/<iteration>_runtimeresults.json and <iteration>_runtimeperview.json; PSNR on batched (1,3,H,W) clamped to [0,1]; SSIM (3DGS) and skimage SSIM; LPIPS alex and vgg.
test_rendering.known_defect: test.py:142 calls sk_ssim(rendernumpy, gtnumpy, multichannel=True). scikit-image removed `multichannel` in 0.23 and requires an explicit data_range for float input. sk_ssim is called BEFORE save_image, so an unpatched crash there prevents the PNGs being written.

preprocessing_pipeline.default_frame_range: --startframe 0 --endframe 50 (argparse defaults, pre_n3d.py:136-137); frame extraction itself always decodes 0..299 (extractframes default endframe=300, pre_n3d.py:45)
steps: 1. extractframes: cv2.VideoCapture per camXX.mp4 -> <scene>/camXX/<frame>.png (PNG, default compression). OpenCV, not ffmpeg.
3. convertdynerftocolmapdb: poses_bounds.npy -> COLMAP input.db + manual/{cameras,images,points3D}.txt, PINHOLE, cx=W//2, cy=H//2, camera order = sorted(glob('cam*.mp4'))
preprocessing_pipeline.how_many_frames_are_triangulated: one COLMAP triangulation per FRAME in [startframe, endframe). A 50-frame model at colmap_0 needs colmap_0..colmap_49; all 300 frames need 300 COLMAP runs and six models (colmap_0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250).

loader_requirements.poses_bounds_npy: REQUIRED at the scene root. dataset_readers.py:83 loads <scene>/poses_bounds.npy and uses it ONLY for near = bounds.min()*0.95 and far = bounds.max()*1.05. Intrinsics and extrinsics come from COLMAP sparse/0.
loader_requirements.per_frame_images: dataset_readers.py:162 builds each frame's path by string-replacing colmap_<starttime> with colmap_<j>, so every frame's colmap_<j>/images/ must exist.
loader_requirements.points: dataset_readers.py:825-830 concatenates colmap_<i>/sparse/0/points3D.bin for i in [starttime, starttime+duration) with a normalized time channel into sparse/0/points3D_total<duration>.ply.
loader_requirements.can_it_take_poses_bounds_plus_a_point_cl: NO. The reader reads COLMAP binaries for cameras/images and one points3D.bin PER FRAME. There is no code path that consumes poses_bounds.npy plus a single ply, so the per-frame COLMAP step cannot be skipped for this baseline.

environment_traps_found: Leonardo COMPUTE nodes have NO outbound network: pip fails with '[Errno 101] Network is unreachable'. The venv and all wheels must be created on the LOGIN node (install_stg_login.sh); only the CUDA builds run in the GPU job.

LD_PRELOAD of the gcc-12.2.0 libstdc++.so.6 is required, mirroring exp_index/leonardo_env.sh. Prepending its lib64 to LD_LIBRARY_PATH is NOT enough: a gcc-runtime-8.5.0 libstdc++ still wins and every vendored extension raises "version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found".

TWO separate LPIPS downloads must be pre-cached into TORCH_HOME from the login node: the torchvision alexnet/vgg16 backbones, AND the LPIPS linear-layer weights that lpipsPyTorch/modules/utils.py:13-17 fetches from raw.githubusercontent.com via torch.hub. Caching only the backbones is insufficient and killed the first render after training had already succeeded.

hunks: test.py:142 sk_ssim(..., multichannel=True) -> sk_ssim(..., channel_axis=2, data_range=1.0). REQUIRED: sk_ssim is called before save_image, so the crash prevents any PNG being written.

thirdparty/gaussian_splatting/utils/general_utils.py safe_state(): seed read from the STG_SEED environment variable, default 0 = upstream behaviour. REQUIRED for a two-seed design: STG hard-codes seed 0 and exposes no --seed flag.

adags_deviations_recorded: Derived frames are 1352x1014, so COLMAP SIFT sees half the linear resolution the published pipeline gives it. Fewer features per frame -> a different (smaller) per-frame triangulated cloud than the published run. Unavoidable: the absence edit exists only at 1352x1014.
config resolution:1 instead of 2, with --downscale 2 in the db conversion; this MATCHES the published effective raster rather than departing from it.
mp4 files are symlinked in from the original scene purely so convertdynerftocolmapdb can recover camera-name order; they are never decoded.

NumPy 2.0: thirdparty/colmap/pre_colmap.py:96 calls ndarray.tostring() and :143 uses np.NaN. Both were removed in NumPy 2.0. prep_derived.py monkey-patches them at run time rather than editing the pinned checkout; envs/stg pins numpy<2 so STG's own import chain (helper_train -> script.pre_immersive_distorted -> thirdparty.colmap.pre_colmap) is unaffected.
mmcv is stubbed in envs/stg (helper_model.py:27 imports it at module level; only ours_lite preprocesspoints==3 calls it).
